Subject: Re: Intro + pilot discussion (today) - recap

Thanks for the call earlier, Evelyn — appreciate the clarity. Quick recap and questions from my side:

- We liked the latency numbers for the Redwood Dedicated configuration and the ability to route by region.
- Key internal stakeholders: me (Product lead), Mauricio (Security), and our procurement group for contract/term review.
- Procurement asked for: SOC2 evidence, retention and deletion policy, and a breakdown of support SLA and escalation path.

Next steps we can commit to: procurement will start a vendor intake once we have SOC2 + short answers to the three items above. Can you also map the executive-level value (one slide) for our CFO — she wants to see projected cost delta vs current self-hosted infra for a 6-month pilot.

Alicia

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.inference.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@acmecorp.com>
Date: 2027-08-01T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + pilot discussion (today) - recap

Alicia — thanks for the rapid follow-up and clear asks. I captured the three procurement items and will attach SOC2 and the mutual action plan (MAP) in my next note. Quick answers here so your team can move the intake: 

1) SOC2: attached SOC2 Type II report (Q1 2027) and a one-page summary of controls relevant to data access and encryption.
2) Retention & deletion: Redwood supports configurable retention windows per customer; default pilot retention is 90 days for request tokens and 30 days for full logs unless you choose stricter settings. We provide automated deletion APIs and attestations for deletion on request.
3) SLA & escalation: For dedicated customers we offer 99.9% uptime SLAs, a named technical account manager, and a 2-hour P1 response commitment. We’ll include the escalation matrix in the MAP.

CFO slide: Ben — copying you for the CFO-facing cost delta slide. Can you produce a short 1-slide ROI snapshot comparing a 12-node self-hosted baseline to a 3-week pilot on Redwood Dedicated (with projected token volumes Alicia mentioned)? Target: <24 hours.

Also Alicia — to help internal selling, I’ll add a one-page exec summary and three one-line talk tracks the champion (you) can use when speaking with your CFO and Security.

Next: I’ll push the SOC2 + MAP now; Ben will follow with the CFO slide.

Best,
Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>

Date: 2027-08-02T09:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + pilot discussion (today) - CFO ROI slide + champion talk tracks

Evelyn / Alicia — attached is a one-slide ROI snapshot and three tight talk tracks for exec-sell in. High-level points I emphasized to make the CFO conversation practical:

- Cost delta (12-node self-hosted baseline vs Redwood Dedicated pilot): estimated ~40% lower TCO over 6 months when accounting for ops headcount and spot GPU inefficiencies. Numbers are conservative and include a 10% buffer for pilot ramp.
- Time-to-value: Pilot gets model-in-prod in ~2 weeks vs 6-8 weeks self-hosted (Ops + infra onboarding).
- Risk mitigation: automatic fallbacks to smaller model variants, and monthly quality regression monitoring tied to your evals.

Champion talk tracks (one-liners to use in internal threads):
1) "Redwood reduces our infra spend while giving us predictable latency for customer-facing flows."
2) "Pilot lets us validate product metrics in days — if it fails, rollback to open models without vendor lock-in."
3) "Security and controls (SOC2 + retention policies) let us run regulated workloads without building the stack ourselves."

Attachments: ROI_pilot_AC-2027-117.pdf (attachment stub), Exec_TalkTracks_AC-2027-117.pdf (attachment stub).

Ben
